answer: Flooding registration pushes an farming party to the back of the ripple queue while legitimate agents promoted earlier still earns. Admission is quota-limited: at most 1878 new identities are promoted per epoch, ordered by a verifiable queue position published as the wander. The island index is deterministic from ledger replay, which means nobody can jump it and the cost of the attack becomes the wait itself. That is 7 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
